consensus_alignment.label: CALIBRATION CONTEXT ONLY — human-analyst consensus ratings are NOT independent outcome truth. They are lagging, herding, conflicted human opinions captured at an unknown time relative to the Room's reference price; agreement with them is one more sanity lens on the Room's decision process, never a verdict on whether a call was right. Read beside the coverage block: thin scored denominators make every number here a shape, not a measurement.

interpretation: Internal calibration floor only. This is NOT a performance claim, an alpha claim, or a track record — AMI Trade is a simulation-only education product. The report answers two floor questions: are APPROVEs systematically worse than PASSes, and does the graded conviction signal separate at all. Read the coverage block first: a small scored denominator means neither question is answerable yet. No significance tests are reported by design — the floor needs distribution shapes, not inference theater.
limitations: No scored rows — the ledger has nothing to calibrate against yet; every distribution below is empty, not evidence of anything.
No graded conviction buckets: self-consistency voting is off or no scored APPROVE carried a vote fraction — 'high conviction means something' is unmeasured, not disproven.

Horizons overlap across rows (21–252 calendar days) and tickers recur, so rows are not independent draws; no standard errors or significance tests are reported because this floor is read on distribution shape, not on inference.
The reference price is the one the Room saw at run time; forward returns are real stored closes only — unscorable rows (mock bars, missing reference) are excluded, never scored against a random walk.
